quizzes.title: Getting Started Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Introduction to C; Variables, Types & Input/Output; Operators & Conditions.

questions.prompt: Which command compiles hello.c into a program called hello?
questions.explanation: gcc is the compiler. The -o option names the output file, so gcc hello.c -o hello creates the program hello.

questions.code:
int a = 7, b = 2;
printf("%d\n", a / b);
questions.explanation: Both a and b are int, so C throws away the decimal part. 7 / 2 gives 3.

questions.prompt: Which line correctly reads an int into the variable age?
questions.explanation: scanf needs the address of the variable, so you write &age. %d is the specifier for int.
A char is a small number. %c shows the letter and %d shows its code, which is 65 for 'A' in ASCII.

questions.prompt: Fill in the operator that tests whether x is equal to 5.
questions.explanation: Use == to compare. A single = assigns a value instead of comparing.

questions.prompt: What happens if you forget break at the end of a switch case?
options: The program keeps running into the next case
Only the first case ever runs
questions.explanation: Without break C falls through and runs the code of the next case too. This is called fall-through.
i starts at 0 and the loop continues while i < 3, so it prints 0, 1 and 2.

questions.prompt: How many times does the body of this loop run?
questions.explanation: A do-while loop runs the body first and checks the condition afterwards, so it always runs at least once.
C passes arguments by value. The function changes its own copy, so a in main is still 5.

questions.prompt: What is the value of sizeof(s) here?
questions.explanation: The string "Hi" has 2 letters plus the null terminator '\0', so the array has 3 bytes.

questions.prompt: Fill in the return type of a function that returns nothing.
questions.explanation: void means the function does not return a value.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct way to check that two strings have the same letters?
questions.explanation: The == operator compares addresses, not letters. strcmp returns 0 when the two strings are equal.
p points to x, so *p = 8 changes x itself. x is now 8.
Adding 2 to p moves it two items forward, so *(p + 2) is a[2], which is 30.

questions.prompt: sp is a pointer to a struct Student. How do you read its roll member?
questions.explanation: Use the arrow -> with a pointer to a struct. sp->roll means the same as (*sp).roll.

questions.prompt: You called int *nums = malloc(5 * sizeof(int)); What should you do when you no longer need the memory?
questions.explanation: Memory from malloc must be given back with free. Otherwise the program has a memory leak.

questions.prompt: Fill in the file mode that adds text to the end of a file without erasing it.
questions.explanation: Mode "a" means append. Mode "w" would empty the file first.

questions.prompt: What does fopen return when it cannot open the file?
questions.explanation: fopen returns NULL on failure, so always check the result before you use the FILE pointer.
